sections.name: PlanetMetric
sections.title: Planet data shape
sections.what: Defines the fields a planet needs: name, module key, item count, health state, orbit distance and speed, icon and the tab it opens.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed description so the parent screen and this planet agree on what data a planet has.
sections.watch_out: Adding a required field here means every place that builds a planet must supply it.

sections.name: SolarPlanetNode (part 1)
sections.title: Health colours, labels and size
sections.what: Defines three looks for a planet: needs attention (red), steady (amber) and thriving (green), each with a label. The planet's size grows with its item count and is kept between 32 and 56 pixels.
sections.why: Likely reason: colour gives a quick health read without needing text.
sections.watch_out: Only the three expected health names are handled, so any other value would break the colour lookup.

sections.name: SolarPlanetNode (part 2)
sections.title: Spinning planet and hover label
sections.what: Spins the planet around the centre continuously, keeps its icon upright, enlarges it on hover, and shows a tooltip with the name, health label, item count and a View Module link. Clicking the planet opens its tab.
sections.why: Likely reason: an orbit-style map where each area is also a button.
sections.watch_out: Very short orbit durations make the planets spin very fast, which may be uncomfortable for some users.

summary: One planet on the life map: a coloured circle that orbits the centre, shows an icon and a tooltip, and opens its life area when clicked.
purpose: Represents one life area (such as Finance) as a clickable planet whose color and speed show its status.
why: Likely reason: a visual, game-like way to show each area's health and activity.
how: The component receives planet data and a starting angle. It picks a color set for the health state and a size from the item count. It places the planet on its orbit ring, keeps the icon upright while the planet spins, and shows a tooltip on hover. Clicking calls the navigation function with the planet's tab name.
inputs: A planet record (name, item count, health state, orbit radius, orbit speed, icon, tab name), the starting angle, and the navigation function.
outputs: A visual planet. Clicking it changes the active tab in the app. Nothing is saved.
risks: An unknown health state would fail the colour lookup. Very short orbit durations spin the planets fast, which may be uncomfortable. Some classes such as negative margins do nothing and are noise.
debug: If a planet has no colour, check that its health state is one of the three expected values. If clicks do nothing, check the navigation function and the tab name. If the planet does not spin, check the orbit duration value.
